faq.q: How long is the DNA in one cell?
faq.a: If all 46 DNA molecules in one human cell were stretched out end to end, they would measure roughly 2 metres.
asks: How much DNA is in a cell?

faq.a: A chromosome is one long DNA molecule wound tightly with proteins. Humans have 46 in most cells, in 23 pairs.
Histones are small proteins that DNA wraps around, like thread on a spool. They help pack DNA neatly and control which genes can be read.
asks: Tell me about the histone beads

faq.a: It is the shape of DNA: two long strands twisted around each other like a spiral ladder. The sides are sugar and phosphate; the rungs are pairs of bases.
asks: Tell me about the double helix

faq.a: The rungs of the DNA ladder. Each rung is two bases joined: adenine with thymine, or cytosine with guanine. Their order spells out the genetic code.

facts: The DNA in a single human cell would be about 2 metres long if stretched out.
The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs in each set of chromosomes.

quiz.say: What does DNA wrap around to stay neatly packed?
quiz.show: What does DNA wrap around to stay neatly packed?
quiz.why: DNA winds around histone proteins like thread on a spool.

wrong.1: Ribosomes make proteins in the cytoplasm; they do not pack DNA.
wrong.2: Mitochondria release energy; nuclear DNA does not wrap around them.

quiz.say: Which list goes from biggest to smallest?
quiz.show: Which list goes from biggest to smallest?
quiz.why: The nucleus holds chromosomes, and each chromosome is made of DNA with base pairs.

wrong.2: Chromosomes sit inside the nucleus, so the nucleus is bigger.
